_comment: Single source of truth for how a calc expression coerces a referenced field value to a number. Asserted by BOTH the JS engine (tests/js/calcParity.test.mjs → javascript/totalform/number-parse.mjs, used by calc.js) and the PHP engine (tests/Unit/Domain/Object/Service/CalcCoercionParityTest.php → src/Domain/Object/Service/CalcService.php) against the same cases. Calc runs twice — live in the browser and again on save — so a value the two engines read differently shows one total on screen and stores another. Add a case here whenever you change coercion in either engine; the other engine's test fails until it matches, which is how drift is caught. Each case evaluates the expression '${v}' with 'value' bound to v, and asserts 'equals'.

cases.name: numeric string, trailing zeros are decimals not grouping
text with a leading digit is not a number
version string is not a number
